But when they were caught between the galleasses, these began in earnest to drive the heaviest pieces of artillery at them, fired again and again, with utter ruin and wreckage of the enemy galleys. And the destruction and scattering of the Turkish fleet was the greater because, as their line had to pass those six galleasses to come and attack the Christian fleet, they suffered more from the contrary wind, which, growing ever fresher, slowed their passage through so thick a storm of the heaviest cannon-shot and blinded them by carrying all the smoke into their faces. This gave the valiant gunners of the galleasses time to scatter a third of the fleet with an endless number of dead and wounded, besides throwing it into complete disorder. Our men then saw a horrible wreckage of masts and yards, galleys broken across, many sinking to the bottom, others burning, some left without oars, drifting, endless people scattered over the water; the whole sea was already covered with men, yards, oars, oar-banks, casks, barrels and every kind of gear. It is incredible that such destruction came from six galleasses alone, never tried before in a naval battle; and they did not stop, turning now with their bows, now with their right side, now with their left, and with their sterns, from continuing so horrible and perpetual a storm.
units.note: Kâtip Çelebi: 'At once six infidel ships came out alone', and the Ottoman galleys, busy with them, were surrounded (Tuhfe Lep. [7]); Uluç Ali had warned that the galleasses were 'like fortresses and batteries' (Tuhfe Lep. [6]). Contarini's 'a third of the fleet' is the Venetian claim for its new weapon.

units.orig: dalla quale Meemet Sirocco, che guidaua il destro corno nimico, volendosi saluare, si separò dalla battaglia, & dal resto dell'armata, & se ne veniua costeggiando il terreno ad incontrare il corno sinistro Christiano, comandato da Agostino Barbarigo, il quale animosamente se gli spinse contra, & con bellissima ordinanza piegando all'auantaggio d'vn monte detto Malcantone, occupò la via all'inimico, & serrogli il passo talmente, che non vna galea, ma vna picciol barca non haurebbe potuto passare. Marino Contarini nipote di esso Barbarigo, qual staua in soccorso del detto Corno, veduto tutta la carica delle galee Turchesche venir contra suo Zio, guidato da troppo valore, & spinto dall'empito del sangue si cacciò auanti, & qui si attaccò crudele & mortal battaglia da gli horribili colpi dell'artiglierie dall'vna & l'altra parte.
units.en: From this storm Mehmed Scirocco, who led the enemy's right wing, wishing to save himself, separated from the centre and the rest of the fleet and came along the coast to meet the Christian left wing, commanded by Agostino Barbarigo. Barbarigo boldly pushed against him and, bending in the finest order to take the advantage of a mountain called Malcantone, blocked the enemy's way and shut the passage so tightly that not a galley, not even a small boat, could have passed. Marino Contarini, Barbarigo's nephew, who was in support of that wing, seeing the whole weight of the Turkish galleys coming against his uncle, led by too much valour and driven by the impulse of his blood, thrust himself forward; and here a cruel and deadly battle began with horrible artillery fire from both sides.

units.orig: Stauano il Corno sinistro, guidato da Oluzali, & il destro Christiano comandato dal Doria, per acciuffarsi insieme, ma amenduni valorosi Capitani per la molta esperienza loro nelle guerre nauali, s'atteneuano cercando ciascun di loro l'auantaggio, ma molto diuersamente: Oluzali teneua i suoi sù l'ale aspettando pur di vedere doue, & a qual parte piegasse la vittoria, & il Doria si trattenea conoscendo il disauantaggio c'haueua, non hauendo egli nel suo corno se non cinquantatre galee, & il nimico nonanta; però dubitandosi non esser colto di mezo, se ne staua sù l'auiso, & così tenendo in dubio l'inimico, seguitato da molte galee si scostò per spacio di vno miglio dal resto del suo corno.
units.en: The [Ottoman] left wing, led by Uluç Ali, and the Christian right, commanded by Doria, were about to grapple, but both valiant captains, from their long experience in the wars at sea, held back, each seeking the advantage, but very differently: Uluç Ali kept his men on the wings, waiting to see where and to which side victory would lean; and Doria held back knowing his disadvantage, having only fifty-three galleys in his wing and the enemy ninety. Fearing to be caught in the middle, he stayed on his guard, and so, keeping the enemy in doubt, he moved off, followed by many galleys, a mile from the rest of his wing.
units.note: Doria's manoeuvre opened the gap that Uluç Ali later used. The Ottoman accounts praise Uluç Ali for exactly this waiting (Tuhfe Lep. [8]).

units.orig: Nella battaglia Reale Gio. d'Austria, il Colonna, & il Veniero con il loro squadrone vnitamente andarono ad incontrar quelle della battaglia del nimico, & le artiglierie de i Christiani sì in essa battaglia come corni, inanti che le galee s'abbordassero insieme, furono scaricate due, tre, & chi cinque volte, & specialmente i cannoni di Corsia, che fu di grandissimo spauento, graue esterminio, & molto impedimento a inimici, in tanto che non potero dar fuogo a molti pezzi, che poi furono trouati essere ancora carichi: & di quelli che sparorono, molti non fecero danno a Christiani, perche le proue delle galee Turchesche erano tanto alte più delle Christiane, che le bocche abbassate fin sù i speroni, portauano ancora tant'alto, che cimauano di sopra le pauesate delle galee Christiane. Con tutto questo i nimici arrabbiati vennero con estremo sforzo di valore ad abbordarsi con i Christiani, che pur animosamente con gridi di vittoria li spingeuano contra, & qui fu vna mortale tempesta d'archibugiate, & di freccie, oltra che parea che ardesse il mare da i lampi & fiamme continoue dei fuochi che erano accesi, con trombe, gettati con pignatte & altri diuersi strumenti. Si erano serrate insieme tre galee a quattro, quattro a sei, & sei ad vna sì delle inimiche come delle christiane tutti combattendo crudelissimamente per non lasciar l'vno la vita all'altro, & già erano saliti sù molte galee di questa e quella parte, Turchi e Christiani combattendo insieme ristretti alla battaglia dell'arme curte, dalla quale pochi restarono in vita, & infinita era la mortalità che vsciua da i spadoni, scimitarre, mazze di ferro, cortelle, manarini, spade, freccie, archibugi, & fuochi artificiati, oltra quelli, che per diuersi accidenti spenti, ritirandosi, & da loro gettandosi s'affogauano in mare, qual già era spesso & rosso di sangue.
units.en: In the royal centre Don John, Colonna and Venier with their squadron went together to meet those of the enemy's centre. The Christian artillery, in the centre as in the wings, was discharged two, three and some five times before the galleys boarded one another, especially the bow guns, which caused very great terror, heavy destruction and much hindrance to the enemy, so that they could not fire many pieces, which were afterwards found still loaded; and of those they fired, many did the Christians no harm, because the bows of the Turkish galleys were so much higher than the Christian that, even with the muzzles lowered to the spurs, they still carried so high that they passed over the pavisades of the Christian galleys. For all this the enraged enemy came on with an extreme effort of valour to board the Christians, who boldly drove against them with cries of victory; and here there was a deadly storm of arquebus shot and arrows, besides which the sea seemed to burn from the flashes and continual flames of the fires that were lit, with fire-trumpets, and thrown in pots and other instruments. Three galleys had closed with four, four with six, and six with one, enemy and Christian alike, all fighting most cruelly so as to leave each other no life; and already many had climbed on to galleys of this side and that, Turks and Christians fighting together at close quarters with short weapons, from which few remained alive; and endless was the slaughter that came from two-handed swords, scimitars, iron maces, knives, hatchets, swords, arrows, arquebuses and fireworks, besides those who, by various accidents, were knocked down, drew back or threw themselves over and were drowned in the sea, which was already thick and red with blood.
units.note: The high Ottoman bows and the League's low firing are a point on which Christian and Ottoman accounts agree in effect: Peçevî and Kâtip Çelebi give the Kapudan's charge and the boarding of his bastarda (Peç. Battle [7]; Tuhfe Lep. [7]).

units.orig: Già Sirocco condottiere del corno destro del Turco, hauendo nel sinistro de Christiani ritrouato gagliardo & valoroso incontro, nè più potendo essequir quanto hauea dissegnato, anzi vedendosi spezzar alberi, puppe, leuar in aria le sbarre banchi & palamenti, con horrenda mortalità de suoi, faceua ogni sforzo di tenerli in battaglia, quando alla fine molte galee di esso cercando di saluarsi da tanta strage, precipitosamente diedero in spiaggia procurando molti col gettarsi a nuoto di saluarsi in terra, alcuni altri chi feriti, chi altramente impediti, & chi per non saper nuotare, s'atteneuano ponendo ogni speranza di salute nella misericordia & clementia di Christiani. Questa fu antica disciplina, che già è penetrata in costume e natura de Turchi, di adoperar nel primo empito & assalto ogni ferità & gagliardia, ma trouando incontro valoroso & forte, di auilirsi & mettersi in fuga. Et inuero qui non sperauano da banda niuna soccorso di soperchieuole numero di gente, qui non aspettauano infinita quantità di caualli, che li spalleggiasse, onde non potendo resistere al valore de' Christiani, quali saliti già sopra il resto delle galee nemiche vrtauano, tagliauano, & ammazzauano quanti se gli opponeuano contra, restarono in poco tempo d'hora abbandonate le galee de gli inimici da i difensori, & conoscendosi già essere in potere de' nostri, i schiaui Christiani spezzate & schiauate, & tagliate le catene con l'armi che de' proprij Turchi teneuano nelle mani, si vendicauano di tante crudeltà vsateli. Marco Quirini, & Antonio Canale, ch'erano dall'altro capo del corno, si spinsero auanti, ma non potero serrar questo corno nimico così presto, che tutti quelli che erano restati viui non si gettassero all'acqua & fuggissero, essendo però tutte le galee di quel corno prese da' Christiani, quali vendicandosi di tante ferità non lasciauano la vita ad alcun infedele. Morì in questo corno sinistro Marino Contarini, Vicenzo Quirini, & Andrea Barbarigo. Restò ferito a morte Agostino Barbarigo d'vna freciata nell'occhio destro, per laqual immediate perse la fauella, della cui morte si dirà poi al suo luogo. Restò ancora guasto & mal trattato dal fuogo Marco Cigogna.
units.en: Scirocco, leader of the Turk's right wing, having met a strong and valiant opposition in the Christians' left and being no longer able to carry out his design, seeing instead his masts and sterns shattered and the rails, benches and oar-banks blown into the air, with horrible slaughter of his men, was making every effort to keep them fighting, when at last many of his galleys, trying to save themselves from such slaughter, ran headlong on to the beach, many men trying to save themselves by swimming ashore; some others, wounded or otherwise hindered, or unable to swim, held on, putting all their hope of safety in the mercy and clemency of the Christians. This was the ancient discipline, now become the custom and nature of the Turks: to use every savagery and force in the first onset and assault, but, meeting a valiant and strong resistance, to lose heart and take to flight. And indeed here they could hope for no help from any side from overwhelming numbers of men, here they could expect no endless multitude of horsemen to back them. So, unable to resist the valour of the Christians, who had already boarded the rest of the enemy galleys and were striking, cutting and killing all who opposed them, the enemy galleys were in a short time abandoned by their defenders; and the Christian slaves, knowing themselves already in our power, broke and unbolted and cut their chains with the Turks' own weapons that they held in their hands, and took vengeance for so many cruelties done to them. Marco Quirini and Antonio Canale, who were at the other end of the wing, pushed forward, but could not close this enemy wing so quickly that all who were left alive did not throw themselves into the water and flee; all the galleys of that wing, however, were taken by the Christians, who, avenging so many savageries, left no infidel alive. In this left wing Marino Contarini, Vincenzo Quirini and Andrea Barbarigo died. Agostino Barbarigo was mortally wounded by an arrow in the right eye, and lost his speech at once; of his death more will be said in its place. Marco Cigogna was also burned and badly hurt.
units.note: The galleys run aground by the shore are the fifteen ships of Kâtip Çelebi's list, which 'ran aground on the shoal and their men poured into the water' near Anatolikoz (Tuhfe Lep. [9]), and the escape of those who took to the mountain in Peçevî (Peç. Battle [8]).

units.orig: Nella battaglia era Don Gio. d'Austria abbordato con Ali Generale de' Turchi, & altri loro dui Capitani di Fanò, hauendo Ali sopra la sua galea trecento Giannizzeri archibugieri, & cento balestrieri, con le loro scimitarre, iquali valorosamente combatteuano. Don Gio. haueua sopra alla sua Reale quattrocento archibugieri scelti del terzo di Sardegna, sotto il comando di Don Lopes di Figeroa maestro di campo, oltre molti altri gentilhuomini & Signori, i quali tutti vnitamente con estrema gagliardia menauano le mani. Il Colonna instaua con gran cuore per la mortalità che de' nemici si vedeua inanti, d'impatronirsi della galea ch'era seco abbordata: & il Veniero daua alti segni di valoroso Capitano, spingendo addosso alli nemici con gran cuore, che ben a tutti i suoi bisognaua menar le mani, hauendo loro tre Generali sette galee di Fanò ben'in ordine addosso, oltre l'altre galee che sempre sopragiungeuano in aiuto à nemici, quali dauano già molto che fare ai nostri, quando la Patrona Reale, & il Commendator maggiore con le due altre galee Loredana & Malipiera, vedendo il grande empito & assalto contra i suoi generali Capitani, & che molte altre galee gli erano per venire per puppa, si spinsero auanti con tanta brauura, ch'entrati nella maggior carica fecero grande occisione de' nimici, & alla fine i dui coraggiosi guerrieri Loredano & Malipiero penetrati nella folta della battaglia restorono in vna salua d'archibugiate morti sopra le loro corsie, nè perciò i defensori di esse si sgomentorno, anzi infiammati di vendicarsi, parue che raddoppiassero le forze in tanto che rimasero vittoriosi di due galee: & il Veniero, & il Colonna il simile fecero di altre due, quando in vn istesso punto Don Gio. qual solo hauea sostenuto il carico di cinque galee nimiche, & già tre conquistate, essendo stato tre volte con gran mortalità ributtato dalla galea di Ali, hauendola acquistata fino all'arboro, alla fine s'impatronì di tutta, & morto Ali già da ogni lato si sentiuano altissimi gridi di vittoria, quale fin'all'hora, ancor che per auanti fusse da Christiani gridata, era però stata dubbiosa, per la gran mortalità & coraggioso valore di ambe le parti nell'abbordarsi nella battaglia Generale, ma hora non facendo più i Turchi testa, si conosceuano i Christiani vittoriosi & patroni dell'inimico, & all'hora erano i Christiani più solleciti al bottinare & legare l'inimico, che al combattere & ammazzare.
units.en: In the centre Don John was grappled with Ali, general of the Turks, and two more of their lantern captains; Ali had on his galley three hundred Janissary arquebusiers and a hundred archers, with their scimitars, who fought valiantly. Don John had on his Real four hundred picked arquebusiers of the tercio of Sardinia under the command of the maestro de campo Don Lope de Figueroa, besides many other gentlemen and lords, who all together laid about them with extreme vigour. Colonna pressed with great heart, for the slaughter of the enemy he saw before him, to master the galley grappled with him; and Venier gave high signs of a valiant captain, pushing against the enemy with great heart. All their men had to lay about them, the three generals having seven well-armed lantern galleys upon them, besides the other galleys that kept arriving to help the enemy and were already giving our men much to do, when the Patrona Reale and the Comendador Mayor, with the two other galleys, Loredan's and Malipiero's, seeing the great onset and assault against their captains general and that many other galleys were about to come at them by the stern, pushed forward with such bravery that, entering the thickest of the fight, they made great slaughter of the enemy; and at last the two courageous warriors Loredan and Malipiero, having pushed into the press of the battle, were killed by a volley of arquebus shot on their own gangways. Yet their defenders did not lose heart; rather, burning for revenge, they seemed to double their strength, so that they won two galleys; and Venier and Colonna did the same with two others; when at the same moment Don John, who alone had borne the weight of five enemy galleys and had already taken three, having been thrown back three times with great slaughter from Ali's galley, and having taken it as far as the mast, at last mastered the whole of it. Ali being dead, cries of victory were heard on every side, the loudest; until then, although the Christians had cried it before, the victory had been doubtful, because of the great slaughter and courageous valour of both sides in the boarding in the main battle. But now, the Turks no longer making a stand, the Christians knew themselves victorious and masters of the enemy, and then they were more eager to plunder and bind the enemy than to fight and kill.
units.note: Peçevî: the League, knowing the Kapudan by his three lanterns, massed against him; he was martyred and his two sons taken with the bastarda (Peç. Battle [7]). Kâtip Çelebi: two ships took the bastarda between them (Tuhfe Lep. [7]). Contarini does not say how Ali died.

units.orig: Erano morti & fatti prigioni molti personaggi nimici, gran numero di Giannizzeri, & infinita quantità de soldati. Saluaronsi solamente quelli che fino dal principio della battaglia, veduto l'esterminio delle galeazze, si haueuano con fregate & altri piccioli legni saluati, come fece Portau, il quale accortosi della perdita imminente, preso l'auantaggio quanto più celatamente puote, montato sopra vno Caichio si saluò in terra. Restorono de' nostri Capitani di galee morti in questa parte dell'armata che fu la battaglia & il soccorso, Gio. Loredano, Catherino Malipiero, Hieronimo Veniero, Francesco Bono, Gio. Battista Benedetti de Cipri, & Giacomo Tressino Vicentino, & molti feriti, quali furono Gio. Bembo, Theodoro Balbi, & il Prior di Messina, oltre molti altri coraggiosi Caualieri, gentilhuomini, & soldati.
units.en: Many enemy personages, a great number of Janissaries and an endless multitude of soldiers were killed or taken. Only those saved themselves who, from the beginning of the battle, seeing the destruction by the galleasses, had escaped in frigates and other small craft, as Pertev did, who, seeing the loss coming, took his chance as secretly as he could, got into a caique and saved himself ashore. Of our captains of galleys there died in this part of the fleet, the centre and the reserve, Giovanni Loredan, Caterino Malipiero, Girolamo Venier, Francesco Bon, Giovanni Battista Benedetti of Cyprus and Giacomo Trissino of Vicenza; and many were wounded, among them Giovanni Bembo, Teodoro Balbi and the Prior of Messina, besides many other courageous knights, gentlemen and soldiers.
units.titel: Pertev escapes; the dead of the centre
units.note: Pertev's escape in all three accounts: in a caique (Contarini), on foot into the mountains (Peç. Battle [7]), fished from the sea and dressed in a servant's clothes (Tuhfe Lep. [7]).

units.orig: Oluzali Capitano del Corno destro [sic] conosciuta c'hebbe la perdita della giornata, & accortosi che il Doria suo auuersario, qual si haueua auueduto dell'auenturoso fine, poteua inuestirlo, vedutosi in auantaggio, & ben considerato quello doueua fare a saluarsi, si spinse con molte galee verso alcune sbandate ch'erano di prima con il Doria, & iui fece grandissimo impeto, & fu da nostri valorosamente sostenuto & incontrato arditamente, non che si confidassero nelle poche forze c'haueano, ma sì ben nella fermissima speranza di soccorso, qual però non hebbero a tempo, essendosi il Doria con le galee sbandato, & troppo allargato, per hauer con buon disegno pigliata la volta per proa della galeazza Pisana per coglier Oluzali dietro alle spalle, il quale auuedutosi che già il Doria era piegato verso a lui con altre vittoriose galee sì della battaglia come del corno sinistro lasciò l'horribile & superchieuole battaglia a quelle poche galee, le quali sole non potendo resistere a così gagliardo assalto restorno malamente trattate, & se ne fuggì in mare con molte altre galee hauendo preso a remurchio & condutto seco le galee di Pietro Bua Corfiotto, del Prior di Messina, & di Luigi Cipico da Traù. In questo conflitto Benedetto Soranzo sempre combattendo senza far stima de tre frecciate c'hauea nella faccia, alla fine non hauendo potuto resistere, che il nimico non si impatronisse della sua galea, che hauea egli con pochi huomini seco per buon pezzo difesa, vi lasciò la vita in sacrificio di Christo & della patria sua, nè gli inimici andarono senza vendetta del fuogo, che acceso nelle monitioni li gittò nell'aria, nè pur si seruò la galea, che poi si vide abbruciata fin'al corbame che radeua con l'acqua. Morì anco Hieronimo Contarini, Marc'Antonio Lando, Marc'Antonio Pasqualigo, Giacomo di Mezo, Giorgio Cornaro, & Pietro Bua sopraditto. De' mal trattati & feriti a morte fu Aluigi Cipico da Traù, il quale essendo ferito di sette graui ferite hauendo combattuto con alquante galee nemiche, indebolito restò con sei soli suoi vinto, ma l'aiuto del soccorso per lui, & per il Prior di Messina fu assai a tempo, che si recuperorno le galee del Prior di Messina, & di esso Luigi Cipico da Traù, che da Oluzali già erano menate via, & furono tutti dui ritrouati malamente viui. Furono mal trattate in questo superchieuole assalto di Oluzali, oltra le predette, vna galea di Sauoia, vna di Fiorenza, & vna Ponentina, & molte altre sì in questo assalto come ne gli altri, ma ancorche molti fussero morti & feriti, tanto però fu il valore de Christiani, & il fauor di Dio, che restorno salue le galee eccetto quella di Pietro Bua Corfiotto, qual fu menata via da nimici.
units.en: Uluç Ali, captain of the right [sic] wing, when he knew the day was lost and saw that Doria, his adversary, who had perceived the fortunate outcome, could attack him, finding himself at an advantage and having well considered what he must do to save himself, pushed with many galleys toward some scattered ones that had been with Doria before, and made a very great onset there. He was valiantly withstood and boldly met by our men, not that they trusted in the few forces they had, but in the firmest hope of help, which they did not have in time, Doria having scattered his galleys and stood out too far, having with a good design gone round the bow of the Pisani galleass to catch Uluç Ali from behind. Uluç Ali, seeing that Doria had already turned toward him with other victorious galleys, both of the centre and of the left wing, left the horrible and overwhelming fight with those few galleys, which, alone and unable to resist so strong an assault, were badly mauled; and he fled out to sea with many other galleys, having taken in tow and carried off the galleys of Pietro Bua of Corfu, of the Prior of Messina and of Luigi Cipico of Traù. In this fight Benedetto Soranzo, fighting on without regard for three arrows in his face, at last unable to prevent the enemy from taking his galley, which he had defended for a long time with few men, gave his life in sacrifice for Christ and his country; nor did the enemy go without the vengeance of fire, which, catching in the powder, blew them into the air; not even the galley was saved, which was afterwards seen burned to the frames at the waterline. There died also Girolamo Contarini, Marc'Antonio Lando, Marc'Antonio Pasqualigo, Giacomo di Mezzo, Giorgio Cornaro and the said Pietro Bua. Among the badly hurt and mortally wounded was Luigi Cipico of Traù, who, having received seven grave wounds fighting several enemy galleys, weakened, was left beaten with only six of his men; but help came in good time for him and for the Prior of Messina, so that the galleys of the Prior of Messina and of Luigi Cipico, which Uluç Ali was already carrying off, were recovered, and both men were found barely alive. In this overwhelming assault of Uluç Ali a galley of Savoy, one of Florence and one from the West were also badly mauled, besides those named, and many others in this and the other assaults; but although many were killed and wounded, such was the valour of the Christians and the favour of God that the galleys were saved, except that of Pietro Bua of Corfu, which the enemy carried off.
units.note: Contarini's 'Prior of Messina' commanded the galleys of the Knights of Malta; Cervantes's captive says Uluç Ali took 'the leading Maltese galley, only three knights being left alive in it' (DQ I.39 [3]), and Kâtip Çelebi that he took the captain of Malta (Tuhfe Lep. [8]). Contarini has the Maltese galley recovered and only Pietro Bua's lost; the Ottoman side brought the standard of the Order back to Istanbul (DQ I.39 [4]). The print calls Uluç Ali's the right wing here, against its own order of battle above.

units.orig: & per la diuina potentia a hore XXI in circa rimase del tutto l'inimico rotto, soggiogato, & vinto: in modo tale, che senza colpo di spada si prese tutto il resto dell'armata Turchesca, eccetto quelle di Oluzali, il qual per il molto auantaggio che lui fuggendo haueua in mare, & perche già poco giorno vi auanzaua non fu seguitato, tutto il resto si rendeua a chi prima gli andaua contra. Spauentoso & horribile spettacolo era il vedere tutto il mare sanguinoso che sospingeua infiniti corpi morti, & compassioneuole a risguardar molti appresi a diuerse sorti di legni andar per il mare, molti mal viui Christiani & Turchi mescolati, dimandar nell'acque nuotando aiuto, & abbracciati ad vn istesso legno cercar di saluarsi. Da ogni parte gridi, da tutte le bande compassioneuoli voci si sentiuano, & quanto più l'aere si oscuraua, tanto maggiore & più horrendo spettacolo pareua. Poiche furono tutte le galee Turchesche ridotte in poter de Christiani, tutti, andorno bottinando & depredando le inimiche spoglie fino a notte restando il tutto in poter loro.
units.en: And by divine power, at about the twenty-first hour, the enemy was left wholly broken, subdued and beaten, so that the whole rest of the Turkish fleet was taken without a sword-stroke, except Uluç Ali's ships, which were not pursued because of the great lead he had at sea in his flight and because little daylight remained; all the rest surrendered to whoever came against them first. It was a fearful and horrible sight to see the whole sea bloody, driving endless dead bodies; and pitiful to see many clinging to all kinds of wood drifting over the sea, many half-alive, Christians and Turks mixed together, swimming and calling for help in the water, and clinging to the same piece of wood trying to save themselves. On every side cries were heard, from every quarter pitiful voices; and the darker the air grew, the greater and more horrible the sight seemed. When all the Turkish galleys had been brought into the power of the Christians, they all went plundering and looting the enemy spoils until night, everything remaining in their power.
units.note: The twenty-first hour is about three hours before sunset: the battle lasted some four hours, as Contarini says below.

units.orig: Questo fù il successo della maggiore & più famosa battaglia nauale, che dal tempo di Cesare Augusto in quà sia mai seguita, & fu a punto quasi nel medesimo luogo, doue egli vinse Marc'Antonio, essendo quella stata al promontorio Atio, oue al presente è la Preuesa. La sera istessa la vittoriosa armata si ridusse ad alcuni porti Petala & altri lì vicini trionfando delle spoglie Ottomane, strascinando per l'acque i superbi stendardi de gli nemici suoi. Grande veramente & miracoloso è stato questo glorioso fatto, che in quattro hore sole, & quando meno s'aspettaua, si abbassasse l'ali al gran serpe d'Oriente, crudelissima ferità scemata al potente Selim. A hora vna di notte l'armata Christiana, per somma diligentia de i Generali, era tutta ridotta salua in porto, quando a punto si leuò vn rabbioso vento, che fece horrenda & furiosa fortuna di mare, che mai tanta gli habitanti diceuano hauer sentita, qui sicuri attesero à medicar gli feriti, & gli istessi padroni li volsero alloggiar ne i loro propri pizzuoli, vsandogli ogni diligentia & cura possibile. Subito Sebastian Veniero Generale di Venetiani espedì per Venetia Onfrè Giustiniano con la sua galea, con lettere al Senato del felice successo, ch'egli conosceua dalla man di Dio.
units.en: This was the outcome of the greatest and most famous naval battle fought since the time of Caesar Augustus, and it was almost in the very place where he defeated Mark Antony, that battle having been at the promontory of Actium, where Preveza now is. The same evening the victorious fleet withdrew to the harbour of Petala and others nearby, triumphing in the Ottoman spoils and dragging the enemy's proud standards through the water. Great and miraculous indeed was this glorious deed, that in only four hours, and when it was least expected, the wings of the great serpent of the East were clipped, and the most cruel savagery of mighty Selim diminished. At one hour after nightfall the Christian fleet, by the utmost diligence of the generals, was all brought safe into harbour, when just then a furious wind arose and made so horrible and raging a storm at sea that the inhabitants said they had never known one like it. There, safe, they saw to the wounded, and the masters themselves chose to lodge them in their own cabins, using every possible diligence and care. At once Sebastiano Venier, general of the Venetians, sent Onfrè Giustinian to Venice with his galley, with letters to the Senate of the happy outcome, which he acknowledged as from the hand of God.
units.titel: Actium, the storm, and the galley sent to Venice
units.note: Actium (31 BC) lies at the mouth of the gulf of Arta, near Preveza, well to the north of the battle; Contarini's 'almost the very place' is rhetoric. Peçevî: no such battle 'since Noah invented the ship' (Peç. Fleet [1]); each side found its superlative.

sections.blurb: The eulogies of the commanders, the dead by rank and trade, the enemy's losses and the prizes, the division of the spoils by the League's shares, and the arrival of the news in Venice on 19 October.

units.orig: La intelligentissima prudentia de i nostri Generali, la brauura & destrezza de i Capitani in mandar ad effetto, il valore de' Gentilhuomini & soldati nell'essequire, fu così grande in ordinar l'armata, spiar l'essere & l'intentione del nemico, in conoscere & valersi di ogni auantaggio, essortare & spingere a tempo i soldati a così gloriosa impresa, che oltre il fatto di tanta eccelsa vittoria, resterà consecrata alla eternità di tutti gli anni la memoria di Don Gio. d'Austria, figliuolo di Carlo V. inuitissimo Imperadore, Capitano generale della Lega tra sua Santità & Filippo Re di Spagna & Venetiani, che quanto più si contempla il ritratto di questa diuina vittoria, tanto maggiore ogni Christiano conosce l'obligo che ha a Filippo Re Catolico di hauer mandato il fratello. Marc'Antonio Colonna nobilissimo Romano, Generale in questa giustissima guerra di Pio V. santissimo tra quanti Pontefici furono già molti anni. La cui creatione fu indubitatamente da eterno preseruata in quei tempi che più la Chiesa di Christo conquassata dalle ponderose forze del Turco, & de' Luterani, haueua bisogno di sostegno, la cui opera fu tanto cara a Dio, che fu basteuole di ristringere insieme con perpetua vnità la santissima Lega sudetta, onde & questo & quello si può vnitamente chiamare Colonna & sostenimento di tutto il Christianesimo.
units.en: The most understanding prudence of our generals, the bravery and skill of the captains in carrying it out, the valour of the gentlemen and soldiers in executing it, were so great in ordering the fleet, spying out the state and intention of the enemy, knowing and using every advantage, and urging and driving the soldiers in time to so glorious an enterprise, that, besides the deed of so exalted a victory, the memory will remain consecrated to the eternity of all the years of Don John of Austria, son of the most invincible Emperor Charles V, captain general of the League between His Holiness, Philip King of Spain and the Venetians: the more one contemplates the portrait of this divine victory, the greater every Christian knows his debt to be to Philip the Catholic King for having sent his brother. Of Marcantonio Colonna, most noble Roman, general in this most just war of Pius V, the holiest of all the Popes for many years, whose election was without doubt preserved from eternity for the times when the Church of Christ, shaken by the weighty forces of the Turk and of the Lutherans, most needed support; whose work was so dear to God that it sufficed to bind together in perpetual unity the most holy League; so that both the one and the other may together be called the Column and support of all Christendom.
units.note: The pun on Colonna, 'column', is Contarini's. 'Perpetual unity': the League was declared perpetual in its first article (Liga Forces [1]); Venice made its separate peace eighteen months later.

units.orig: Sebastian Veniero Generale della felice & deuota Republica Venetiana il quale mostrò non men la grandezza del cuore nel combattere che somma prudentia nel gouernare, hauendo in questo horrendo conflitto fatto officio & di Generale & di valoroso soldato, non lasciando pur all'inuidia da desiderare cosa alcuna, che in vna così gran giornata fusse bisogneuole per la vittoria, non ha egli meritato vna statua di bronzo, a eterna memoria del suo valore, & specchio come gli altri nobili Venetiani si deueno portare verso la patria? Agostino Barbarigo, il quale vdita la desiata vittoria tre giorni dopo, se ben per la perduta fauella non puote formar parola alcuna, alzate le mani al cielo mostrò segno dell'inuitto suo cuore, & di somma consolatione: & nella morte trionfò di tanto eccelsa impresa, portando seco la palma della vittoria in cielo. I dui Principi di Parma & Vrbino, che nella maggior folta erano, l'vno con Hettor Spinola, l'altro con Monsignor di Leyni diedero eterno testimonio del gran valor loro, essendo restati vittoriosi. Il Commendator maggiore che mai abbandonò sua Altezza, & alla difesa sua sempre assistendo fece cose immortali, dimostrò infinito valore. Il Marchese santa Croce, che con tanta accortezza guidò il soccorso, che sempre con somma celerità si trouò in aiuto di chi era oppresso o superchiato, spiegò viuace essempio del gran cuore, & prudentia sua. Paolo Giordano Orsino, qual era al capo della battaglia, qual più eccelsa grandezza di cuore poteua mostrare, che entrando ne gli nimici seruar se stesso, & vincer tante galee? Il Giustiniano prior di Messina, se ferito non restaua a morte, costretto ritirarsi in pizzuolo, hauendo altre volte dato conto del suo valore, faceua indubitatamente che tanti suoi non moriuano, se ben Oluzali con tanto superchieuole assalto lo combatteua. Marco Quirini & Antonio Canale tutti dui resteranno pur eternamente illustri al mondo per i gloriosi fatti loro in tutta questa guerra, oltre l'esterminio fatto a inimici nella Giornata. Gio. di Cardona capo del corno destro, che era fra le galee mal menate da Oluzali rese tanto chiaro lampo del suo valore nell'hauersi saputo combattendo saluare, quanto questo eterno fatto in vn conflitto tanto superchieuole è più eccelsa gloria, che combattendo del pari & con qualche disauantaggio restarne vittorioso.
units.en: Sebastiano Venier, general of the happy and devout Venetian Republic, who showed no less greatness of heart in fighting than the utmost prudence in governing, having done in this horrible conflict the office both of general and of valiant soldier, leaving even envy nothing to wish for that was needed for victory on so great a day: has he not deserved a bronze statue, to the eternal memory of his valour and as a mirror of how other Venetian nobles ought to bear themselves toward their country? Agostino Barbarigo, who, hearing of the longed-for victory three days later, though he could form no word because he had lost his speech, raised his hands to heaven and showed a sign of his unconquered heart and of the greatest consolation; and in death he triumphed in so exalted an enterprise, carrying the palm of victory with him to heaven. The two princes of Parma and Urbino, who were in the thickest press, the one with Ettore Spinola, the other with Monsieur de Leyni, gave eternal witness of their great valour, remaining victorious. The Comendador Mayor, who never left His Highness and, always at hand for his defence, did immortal things, showed infinite valour. The Marquis of Santa Cruz, who led the reserve with such shrewdness that he was always found with the greatest speed helping whoever was hard pressed or overwhelmed, displayed a lively example of his great heart and prudence. Paolo Giordano Orsini, who was at the head of the centre: what more exalted greatness of heart could he show than, entering among the enemy, to preserve himself and overcome so many galleys? Giustiniani, Prior of Messina, had he not been mortally wounded and forced to withdraw to his cabin, having given proof of his valour at other times, would without doubt have prevented so many of his men from dying, although Uluç Ali fought him with so overwhelming an assault. Marco Quirini and Antonio Canale will both remain eternally famous in the world for their glorious deeds in this whole war, besides the destruction they did to the enemy on the day. Giovanni de Cardona, head of the right wing [sic], who was among the galleys mauled by Uluç Ali, gave as bright a flash of his valour in knowing how to save himself fighting, as this eternal deed, in so overwhelming a conflict, is a higher glory than to win fighting on equal terms or at some disadvantage.
units.note: Venier got his statue: it stands in the church of Santi Giovanni e Paolo in Venice (1907). The praise of the Prior of Messina, Pietro Giustiniani, commander of the Maltese galleys, sits oddly beside Cervantes's and Kâtip Çelebi's report that his galley was taken (Contarini Battle [17]).

units.orig:
La conclusione è, che tutti quelli, che si sono trouati in questo naual conflitto, hauendo combattuto per Christo nostro Signore, & per la patria loro, se viui sono possono gloriarsi di essersi trouati in vn fatto tanto glorioso ad acquistare vna sì eccelsa & immortal vittoria; Se morti sono, trouandosi hora tra beati, godono della eterna gratia fattagli, d'hauer con così breue martirio tramutato le poche hore di vita mortale in sempiterna assistentia presso di Dio, il che deue essere di gran conforto & suprema contentezza dei Padri & parenti loro, sapendo questi ch'essendo mortali non poteuano generare i figliuoli immortali, ma che desiderandoli huomini d'honore, & illustri al mondo, hanno in questo sol punto acquistato l'vno & l'altro con sempiterna gloria loro, che mai li sarà tolta. units.en:
The conclusion is that all who took part in this naval conflict, having fought for Christ our Lord and for their country, if they are alive may glory in having been present at so glorious a deed, winning so exalted and immortal a victory; if they are dead, being now among the blessed, they enjoy the eternal grace given them of having exchanged, by so brief a martyrdom, the few hours of mortal life for everlasting attendance on God; which must be a great comfort and the highest contentment to their fathers and kinsmen, knowing that, being mortal, they could not beget immortal sons, but that, wishing them men of honour and famous in the world, they have in this one moment gained both, with everlasting glory to them that will never be taken away. Their number, as far as could be had from the muster, was 7,656, namely:

Legni de gl'inimici conquistati da Christiani furono 130 cioè galee 117 & galeotte 13 i qual legni furono tutti ridotti la sera in porto con tutte le loro monitioni, la maggior parte cariche di Pane, Pegole, Seui, Butiri, Risi, Faue, & diuerse altre sorti di monitioni & vettouaglie, fornite tutte d'armizi a sufficientia, oltra i quali 130 Vasselli ne restorno in mare tra abbandonati & a fondo, circa 80. le fuggite si giudica 40 in circa. Si fece per la ottenuta Vittoria per tre giorni continui in tutta l'armata feste & allegrezze, laudando ognuno il grande Iddio di sì larga gratia, hauendo tutte le galee per allegrezza con suoni, spiegati ogni sorte di stendardi & bandiere, tutti attendendo a ragunar le sue galee per seguir la cominciata vittoria, ma per i tempi contrarii ritenuti in quei porti fin'alli XV furono costretti dar interuallo sopragiungendo tuttauia la strana stagione del verno, & sempre morendo de gli feriti, per il che sua Altezza vedendo l'impresa disperata, non volse più tardare alla partenza sua per Messina, dando larga speranza l'anno seguente per tempo di nuouo congiungersi, & così deliberati partirono, conducendo seco i vaselli acquistati & spoglie nemiche a Corfù, nel qual luogo di comun volere fu fatta la diuisione in questo modo.
units.en:
Of the enemy, dead and taken, there were 29,990, namely:
Lantern captains — 34
Commanders of galleys — 120
Janissaries, sipahis, volunteers and oarsmen — 25,000
Taken prisoner — 3,846
The enemy vessels taken by the Christians were 130, namely 117 galleys and 13 galliots, which were all brought into harbour that evening with all their stores, most of them laden with bread, pitch, tallow, butter, rice, beans and various other kinds of stores and victuals, all sufficiently furnished with gear. Besides these 130 vessels, about 80 remained at sea, abandoned or sunk; those that fled are reckoned at about 40. For the victory won there were feasts and rejoicing for three days on end in the whole fleet, everyone praising great God for so large a grace, all the galleys in their joy with music and every kind of standard and flag spread, all busy gathering their galleys to follow up the victory begun. But held in those harbours by contrary weather until the fifteenth, they were forced to pause, with the strange winter season coming on and the wounded dying all the time; so His Highness, seeing the enterprise hopeless, would no longer delay his departure for Messina, giving great hope of joining again early the next year; and so resolved they left, taking the captured vessels and enemy spoils with them to Corfu, where by common consent the division was made in this manner.
units.titel: The enemy's losses, and the prizes
units.note: The print's total, 29,990, does not match its own figures, which add up to 29,000. Contarini's 130 taken and 80 sunk make the 210 lost that Peçevî rounds to 190 (Peç. Fleet [1]); Kâtip Çelebi counts sixty taken into the Venetian armoury (Tuhfe Lep. [9]). The forty that escaped are Uluç Ali's squadron. 'Seeing the enterprise hopeless': the victory was not followed up, the first step toward what Cervantes's captive calls the lost opportunity (DQ I.39 [4]).

To His Holiness fell as his portion: 19 galleys, 2 galliots; 19 cannon, 3 stone-throwers, 42 small cannon; 881 slaves
To His Catholic Majesty: 58 galleys, 6 galliots; 58 cannon, 8 stone-throwers, 128 small cannon; 1,713 slaves
To the Most Serene Venetian Republic: 39 galleys, 4 galliots; 39 cannon, 5 stone-throwers, 86 small cannon; 1,162 slaves
units.note: The division follows the League's cost shares: half to Spain, a third to Venice, a sixth to the Pope (Liga Money [3]). The 'slaves' are the Ottoman prisoners, made galley slaves in their turn; the Christian oarsmen freed from the Ottoman galleys, some fifteen thousand by other counts, are not in Contarini's tally. The print sets this as a table; it is given here line by line.

units.orig: Fra questo tempo la galea di Onfrè Giustiniano mandata dal Veniero il dì XIX di Ottobre entrò i dui Castelli di Venetia, oue infinito popolo ridotto sù la piazza di San Marco l'aspettaua tra la tema & la speranza, ma auicinandosi già la felice galea con tanta frequentia di cannonate, & scoperta chiaramente che strascinaua per l'acque molte bandiere Turchesche, & discernendosi molti Christiani vestiti di habiti de' Turchi, empì tutti di grato giubilo & di ferma speranza di qualche auenturoso successo, ma non già di vna sì eccelsa & immortale vittoria, come poi esso il Giustiniano disceso di galea con lettere del General Veniero ne diede particolar conto al Serenissimo Principe Luigi Mocenico, di essersi dissipata e presa tutta l'armata Turchesca con pochissimo danno de Christiani.
units.en: Meanwhile the galley of Onfrè Giustinian, sent by Venier, on 19 October entered between the two castles of Venice, where an endless crowd gathered in the square of San Marco awaited it between fear and hope. But as the happy galley drew near with such continual firing of guns, and it was clearly seen to be dragging many Turkish flags through the water, and many Christians were made out dressed in Turkish clothes, it filled everyone with welcome joy and a firm hope of some fortunate outcome, though not yet of so exalted and immortal a victory, until Giustinian himself, coming down from the galley with General Venier's letters, gave a particular account of it to the Most Serene Prince Alvise Mocenigo: that the whole Turkish fleet had been scattered and taken with very little loss to the Christians.
units.note: The Christians 'dressed in Turkish clothes' are sailors wearing captured clothing. With this galley the printed Lepanto began: the prints, poems and medals that the game counts as 'what was remembered' start in Venice within days (compare Chest. and Fam. Ded.).

units.orig: Per il che subito sua Serenità accompagnata dal Legato di sua Santità, dal Patriarca Grimani, da dui Consiglieri, & da Cesare Ziliolo Cancelliere pur di sua Serenità, quali per altri negocij erano in palazzo ridotti, discese con pochi altri nobili nella Chiesa del Protettor nostro San Marco, oue frequentando tuttauia il Senato, & la Chieresia cominciorono a cantar il Te Deum laudamus, quando poi fu celebrata vna solenne Messa, rendendo ciascuno gratie a N. S. Dio, qual scordatosi tutti i nostri errori per l'ampiezza della sua misericordia, haueua in vn tempo così bisognoso allargata con la potentia del suo braccio immensa vittoria al suo popolo Christiano. Il medesimo giorno diede sua Serenità il carico di far l'oratione à Gio. Battista Rasario, huomo dottissimo, il quale recitandola il terzo giorno seguente nella medema Chiesa di San Marco, lasciò & il Serenissimo Senato pieno delle merauiglie del suo artificio, & l'infinito popolo di tanti nobili forestieri attonito nel stupore del glorioso successo, dell'eloquentia, & della somma sapientia dell'oratore. In tanto per tutta la città non si vdiua, se non giubilosi gridi di vittoria, suoni di campane, vedeansi indistinti abbracciamenti de popoli, & infiniti altri tenerissimi segni d'allegrezza, con chi ognuno rendeua laude al Creatore della tanta & sì larga sua riceuuta gratia. IL FINE.
units.en: At once His Serenity, accompanied by the Legate of His Holiness, the Patriarch Grimani, two Councillors and Cesare Ziliolo, His Serenity's chancellor, who were gathered in the palace on other business, went down with a few other nobles into the church of our Protector Saint Mark, where, with the Senate and the clergy crowding in, they began to sing the Te Deum laudamus; and then a solemn Mass was celebrated, everyone giving thanks to our Lord God, who, forgetting all our errors in the breadth of his mercy, had in so needful a time granted by the power of his arm an immense victory to his Christian people. The same day His Serenity gave Giovanni Battista Rasario, a most learned man, the charge of making the oration, which he delivered on the third day following in the same church of San Marco, leaving the Most Serene Senate full of wonder at his art, and the endless crowd of so many noble foreigners astonished at the glorious outcome and at the eloquence and supreme wisdom of the orator. Meanwhile through the whole city nothing was heard but joyful cries of victory and the ringing of bells; people were seen embracing without distinction, and endless other most tender signs of joy, with which everyone gave praise to the Creator for so great and so large a grace received. THE END.
units.note: Contarini's history ends with the feast in Venice, not with the war. It was printed within months; the peace of March 1573, by which Venice gave up Cyprus, came after it.
